ajay.khan: Heads-up — today's onboarding batch hit a weird failure mode: 3 models passed ingest but started failing runtime smoke with KV cache shape errors after quantization.

kate.chen: ugh. which step exactly? pre-quant or post-quant smoke?

ajay.khan: post-quant smoke. ingest -> convert -> quantize -> export -> smoke-run. failures show mismatch between exported embedding dim and runtime expectation. logs attached.

maria.lopez: can you paste the smoke invocation?

ajay.khan: sure:
```
python infra/smoke/run_smoke.py --model-id rmdl-2026-03-15 --seed 42 --mode postquant --checks kv_shape,forward_sanity
```

sylvain: quick hypothesis: tokenizer vocab shuffling during conversion + tokenizer hashing not tracked -> embedding table reorder, so exported weights dont align with runtime token ids. Seen this before with converter v0.9.

kate.chen: that would explain embedding dim mismatch. converter v0.9 had a fast-path that rewrites tokenizer files if it detects missing tokens.

ajay.khan: onboard-bot posted the failing logs: "ERROR runtime: kv cache shape mismatch expected (8,512,1024) got (8,256,1024)"

ci-bot: CI: smoke-run rmdl-2026-03-15 FAILED (see logs: https://ci.internal/runs/9876) :x:

maria.lopez: two quick questions: 1) Is this a converter bug or an onboarding contract gap? 2) How often would stricter checks block good models?

sylvain: partly converter. partly our contract: we only assert total_vocab_size equality, not token->index mapping or vocab hash. So conversion can be lossy and still pass ingest.

kate.chen: tradeoff: adding token->index equality check (vocab_hash) is cheap and would catch this early. Downside: some community models rely on tokenizer normalization changes and would be blocked unless we add an adapter shim.

ajay.khan: proposal: introduce a 2-stage preflight: cheap signature checks (vocab_size, vocab_hash, config_fingerprint) run inline at ingest, then heavy bench + quantization compatibility runs asynchronously. If cheap checks fail, fail fast and surface converter diff.

maria.lopez: +1. also add a lightweight deterministic conversion mode for onboarding that refuses to rewrite token maps and emits warnings instead. That will help us triage whether converter should change.

sylvain: implementation notes: new check -> compute tokenizer SHA256 of token list file and compare to manifest. add a small shim in converter: `--no-token-reorder` to produce a strict export.

kate.chen: we also need to capture runtime expectations in the model manifest: expected kv cache layout (num_heads, head_dim, hidden_size) and embedding table shape. That way runtime can assert earlier.

ajay.khan: agreed. add fields `expected_vocab_hash`, `expected_kv_shape` to manifest. Update ingest API to reject missing expected_* fields for gated enterprise models, optional for community.

maria.lopez: ops question: will this slow onboarding? if cheap checks run inline it's minimal. Deterministic conversion will be an extra option only run in CI for suspicious models.

sylvain: timeline: I can land the vocab_hash check + manifest fields in the next sprint (2w). I'll followup with a tiny RFC for the converter `--no-token-reorder` flag.

kate.chen: action items: 1) sylvain: implement vocab_hash + manifest schema changes (PR + tests). 2) ajay: add cheap preflight checks to ingest endpoint and update smoke-run to surface converter diffs. 3) maria: update onboarding runbook + failure playbook with this new failure mode.

ajay.khan: I'll file the ingest ticket and add a short checklist to the onboarding doc.

onboard-bot: New ticket created: ONB-4122 "vocab-hash preflight + manifest expected_kv_shape" (assignee: sylvain).

ci-bot: rerun requested by kate.chen — queued.

maria.lopez: one more thought — add a periodic job to re-run deterministic conversion on a sample of community models to detect silent drift between converter versions. low-cost sampling.

sylvain: +1. will add a cron job blueprint in the RFC.

kate.chen: sounds good. if we do this, we can reduce the long tail of runtime failures and speed up resolution. prefer to keep heavy bench async to not throttle pipeline throughput.

ajay.khan: thanks all. I'll summarize and close this thread after tickets land. :)
